# DGMS Statutory Reporting Pack — Serious Reportable Accident

## Underground Coal Mine · Dhanbad Zone, Jharkhand · Mines Act 1952 / Coal Mines Regulations 2017

> **Decision-support only — not legal advice.** This pack is a *draft* for a **DGMS-qualified competent person** (1st-Class Mine Manager's Certificate holder / statutory Manager or Agent) to verify and sign before anything is filed. It resolves the *shape* of the statutory obligation from a legacy-first knowledge base; it does **not** replace the statutory text, a DGMS circular, or the regional office's own instruction. **No form number is invented — anything the knowledge base does not verify is flagged `[GAP]` and routed to the competent person / the regional DGMS office.**

---

## 0 · Region & legal regime — CONFIRMED

| Item | Resolved value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Mine type | **Underground coal mine** | User-supplied |
| Region / zone | **Dhanbad zone, Jharkhand** (as supplied) | User-supplied — treated as confirmed |
| Parent statute | **Mines Act 1952** (OH&S parent statute for mines) | `KB-REG-IN-MINES-ACT` |
| Subordinate regulations | **Coal Mines Regulations 2017 (CMR 2017)** + Mines Rules 1955 | User-supplied regime; consistent with the DGMS coal regime |
| Administering authority | **Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS)**, through its regional / zonal offices | `KB-REG-IN-MINES-ACT`, `KB-REG-IN-DGMS` |
| Filing context | **Regional / zonal** — the correct DGMS regional office of jurisdiction receives the notice | `KB-REG-IN-DGMS` |

**`[GAP] — DGMS regional office of jurisdiction (name / address / postal + electronic routing).`** The knowledge base carries the *regime* (Mines Act 1952 / CMR 2017, DGMS-administered) but **does not carry a DGMS zone → office directory** (state-factory forms ≠ DGMS zones). "Dhanbad zone" is accepted as supplied, but the **exact regional office having territorial jurisdiction over this mine — and its current postal address and electronic-filing address — must be confirmed against the DGMS office directory (dgms.gov.in) or by contacting the regional office directly** before the notice is dispatched. A 24-hour notice routed to the wrong office is a *misfiled* statutory notice.

**OSH-Code transition note (legacy-first).** The Mines Act 1952 is among the 13 labour statutes to be subsumed by the **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**. Consolidation of mines safety under the Code is **state-by-state and still pending**; most mines continue to file the legacy DGMS forms today, and the savings provisions keep legacy filings valid. **File the legacy DGMS artefacts below**; treat the OSH Code as *direction of travel*, not a live consolidated form.

## 1 · De-identification pass (applied BEFORE drafting — MANDATORY)

Accident-notification facts carry the **highest-sensitivity** data (injured / deceased-miner identity and health detail). Before any notice text is drafted or circulated:

**1.1 — Detect & flag** every personal / health identifier in the raw accident record. For a serious coal-mine accident these typically include:

- Injured / deceased worker name(s), father's / spouse's name, address
- Employee / token / PF / ESIC / Aadhaar number
- Exact designation, crew, gang, shift, ticket number
- Nature and body-part of injury, medical / post-mortem detail
- Names of eye-witnesses, the shot-firer, the overman/sirdar, rescue party members
- Photographs, contact numbers

**1.2 — Pseudonymise by default.** Replace each identifier with a **stable role label**: `Injured Person 1`, `Deceased Person 1`, `Witness A`, `Overman on shift`, `Shot-firer`, `Rescue Party Member 1`. Produce (a) the de-identified pack and (b) a **separate re-identification key**. **The key never appears in this document** — store it access-controlled, apart from the pack. *(Note: the statutory notice filed to DGMS will itself require the real identity of the injured/deceased person as prescribed; keep that identified version as a controlled filing copy — this de-identified pack is the circulating / working record.)*

**1.3 — Aggregate small numbers.** Never publish an injury/fatality category with **fewer than 5 individuals** in any widely circulated version; aggregate and apply secondary suppression so a suppressed cell can't be back-calculated from a total.

**1.4 — Warn before wide circulation.** Any version leaving the statutory-filing channel (board note, toolbox brief, notice board) defaults to de-identified / aggregated.

## 3 · Statutory obligations — sequenced by deadline

**Assumed event datetime for the worked timeline:** `4 July 2026, 14:30 hrs` **`[ASSUMPTION — substitute the actual event date & time; every deadline below recalculates from it]`.** If a deadline has already passed when the pack is assembled, **file immediately** and record the reason for delay — do not back-date.

| # | Obligation | To whom (recipient) | Deadline | Legal citation | Form-id | Owner (role) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Notice by the quickest means** (telephone / fax / e-mail / special messenger) that a serious/reportable accident has occurred | DGMS **regional office of jurisdiction** (Dhanbad zone); for a fatal, also the **district authorities** | **Forthwith** — as soon as the accident is known (T+0) | Mines Act 1952 accident-notification duty (`KB-REG-IN-MINES-ACT`); CMR 2017 — **exact section / regulation `[GAP]`** | Not a numbered form; prescribed *instrument*, if any, **`[GAP]`** | Mine Manager (through Agent/Owner as required) | 4 July 2026, forthwith after 14:30 hrs |
| B | **24-hour written accident notice** — the prescribed accident notice | DGMS **regional office of jurisdiction** (Dhanbad zone); additional statutory recipients (e.g. District Magistrate) **`[GAP] — confirm`** | **Within 24 hours** of the event (T+24h) | Mines Act 1952 + CMR 2017 accident-notification duty (`KB-REG-IN-MINES-ACT` → `KB-REG-IN-DGMS`, **verified anchor: 24-hour accident notice**); exact section/regulation **`[GAP]`** | **`(DGMS-prescribed — verify per mine) [GAP]`** — the 24-hour *duty + timing* are verified; the **numbered form is `[GAP]`** | Mine Manager | **by 5 July 2026, 14:30 hrs** |
| C | **Enter the accident in the accident & dangerous-occurrence register** | Internal statutory register (kept at the mine, produced on DGMS inspection) | **On the day; kept current** (T+0) | Mines Act 1952 registers/returns duty (`KB-REG-IN-DGMS`, **verified anchor**) | **Form J** *(verified)* | Mine Manager | 4 July 2026 |
| D | **Site preservation** — do not disturb the scene of a serious/fatal accident until examined by an Inspector or the prescribed period elapses (rescue/safety of persons excepted) | DGMS Inspector (on attendance) | **From T+0 until released** — duration **`[GAP]`** | Mines Act 1952 — **exact section `[GAP]`**; CMR 2017 **`[GAP]`** | Not a form | Mine Manager / Agent | From 4 July 2026 until released by the Inspector |
| E | **Maintain the employee register** (supplies the de-identified personnel facts the notice references) | Internal statutory register (produced on inspection) | **Maintained current** | Mines Act 1952 returns/registers duty (`KB-REG-IN-DGMS`, **verified anchor**) | **Form B** *(verified)* | Mine Manager | Current at 6 July 2026 |
| F | **Annual return** — the accident feeds the mine's accident statistics for the reporting year | DGMS (per the return's routing) | **By ~20 January** of the following year → **by 20 January 2027** (for CY 2026) — *legacy due date* | Mines Act 1952 returns duty (`KB-REG-IN-DGMS`, **verified anchor: annual return ~20 Jan**) | **Annual return** *(verified obligation; a specific numbered return form, if required, is `[GAP]`)* | Mine Manager / Agent | 20 January 2027 |
| G | **Statutory-appointment completeness check** — confirm the Manager (and statutory officials) are validly appointed; the notice is signed *through* the Manager, and a defective appointment weakens the filing | Internal record (produced on inspection) | Standing — confirm before filing | Mines Act 1952 appointment duty (`KB-REG-IN-MINES-ACT` → `KB-REG-IN-DGMS`, **verified anchor**) | **Statutory Manager (+ officials) appointment letter** *(verified)* | Owner / Agent (appoints the Manager) | Confirm by 5 July 2026 |
| H | **Quarterly / other periodic returns beyond the annual** | DGMS | Per DGMS timing **`[GAP]`** | Mines Act 1952 returns duty | **`(DGMS-prescribed — verify per mine) [GAP]`** — only the annual return (~20 Jan) is a verified anchor | Mine Manager / Agent | `[GAP]` |

### Filing sequence in plain language

1. **Immediately (T+0)** — secure persons, render first aid/rescue, **preserve the site** (D), and give **notice by the quickest means** to the DGMS regional office (A). For a fatal, notify the district authorities too.
2. **Within 24 hours (T+24h)** — dispatch the **written 24-hour accident notice** (B) to the confirmed DGMS regional office. *This is the spine obligation.*
3. **Same day, kept current** — record the accident in the **Form J** register (C) and ensure the **Form B** employee register is current (E).
4. **Standing** — confirm the **statutory-appointment** letters are valid (G).
5. **By 20 January 2027** — carry the accident into the mine's **annual return** for CY 2026 (F).
6. **Confirm & schedule** any **further periodic return** the regional office prescribes (H) — do not assume a form; verify it.

## 4 · Legal-citation & form-id register (verified vs `[GAP]`)

**Verified anchors — cited as values (from `KB-REG-IN-DGMS`):**

- ✔ **24-hour accident notice** (serious/fatal/dangerous occurrence) — *duty + 24-hour timing verified*
- ✔ **Form J** — accident & dangerous-occurrence register
- ✔ **Form B** — employee register
- ✔ **Annual return** — by ~20 January (legacy due date)
- ✔ **Statutory Manager (+ officials) appointment letter**

**`[GAP]` — routed to the competent person / regional DGMS office, never invented:**

- ✗ **The numbered form-id of the 24-hour accident notice** → `(DGMS-prescribed — verify per mine) [GAP]`
- ✗ **The exact Mines Act 1952 section number** for the accident-notification duty → `[GAP]`
- ✗ **The exact Coal Mines Regulations 2017 regulation number(s)** for accident notification, site preservation, and the register/return duties → `[GAP]`
- ✗ **The exact Mines Act 1952 section / CMR 2017 regulation** governing **site preservation** and the **duration** the site must be preserved → `[GAP]`
- ✗ **The specific DGMS regional office** of territorial jurisdiction (name / address / electronic-filing route) for the Dhanbad-zone mine → `[GAP]`
- ✗ **Additional statutory recipients** of the accident notice beyond the DGMS regional office (e.g. District Magistrate / local authority) and their exact triggers → `[GAP]`
- ✗ **Any numbered periodic/quarterly return** beyond the annual return → `(DGMS-prescribed — verify per mine) [GAP]`
- ✗ **Whether a Court of Inquiry / special enquiry** is convened (for a fatal or serious dangerous occurrence) and any consequent duty on the mine → `[GAP]`

> Why these are `[GAP]` and not guessed: the knowledge base verifies the *duty and timing* of the five anchors but **not** the numbered forms, section numbers, or the zone office map. Fabricating a plausible number would pass an automated row-blind citation check yet **misdirect a statutory filing** — a fabricated number is worse than an honest `[GAP]`. Resolve each `[GAP]` from the statutory text held by the mine, the DGMS circulars, or the regional office directly.

## 6 · Competent-person review note

This pack is **decision-support**, not legal advice, and is **not a statutory sign-off**. Every `[GAP]` above must be resolved, and the whole pack verified, by a **DGMS-qualified competent person** (statutory Mine Manager / Agent) against the mine's held copy of the **Mines Act 1952**, the **Coal Mines Regulations 2017**, the **Mines Rules 1955**, and current DGMS circulars, and against the **actual DGMS regional office of jurisdiction**, **before any notice, register entry, or return is filed**. Where the class of accident is uncertain (serious vs fatal vs dangerous occurrence), the competent person confirms the classification first — the 24-hour clock and the site-preservation duty both depend on it. When in doubt on any deadline, **notify early**.
